newsitem.title: MEXICO: Six Mexicans arrested for raiding sea turtle nests.
newsitem.headline: Six Mexicans arrested for raiding sea turtle nests.

text.p: Mexican federal agents have arrested six people in Sinaloa and Michoacan states for trafficking eggs of the endangered Golfina sea turtle, the attorney general's office (PGR) said on Wednesday.
Golfina sea turtles come ashore to lay their eggs in nests dug out of sand on Pacific Coast beaches. The eggs are a part of the diet of poor coastal people throughout Mexico and Central America.

"With the goal of preserving and protecting species in danger of extinction, elements of the Federal Judicial Police ... detained six presumed raiders of sea turtle eggs," the attorney general's office said in a news release. "Nearly 7,000 eggs were confiscated."
Two men were arrested while on their way to market in Culiacan, the capital of Sinaloa. The eggs were hidden in a false bottom in the bed of their pickup, the statement said.
In Lazaro Cardenas, a coastal city in Michoacan, authorities arrested four people caught with sea turtle eggs in a fishing boat, the attorney general's office said.
